Nearly 200 major websites hit by supply-chain cyber attack: report

cards.what_happened: A malicious cyber attack targeted nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA. Hackers injected corrupted JavaScript code into Optimizely tools, affecting about 178 sites. The attackers aimed to steal credit card numbers and cryptocurrency and to infect Apple devices.
details: Hackers injected corrupted JavaScript code into tools hosted by Optimizely, a digital platform used by major companies to customize online experiences. This malicious cyber attack targeted nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, as well as Zoom, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock. The attack was reported Tuesday by specialist media.

The attackers sought to steal users’ credit card numbers and cryptocurrency and to upload code to Apple devices for further exploitation. According to security researcher Scott Helme, the attacker’s crypto wallets received about $7,040 within roughly nine hours on November 16. Helme first uncovered the hack and wrote about it on his blog Monday.

Most of the malicious code had been removed from the affected sites, Helme said. Optimizely stated that it identified and contained a security incident affecting some of its Web Experimentation customers. The company added that the vulnerable path was blocked, the injected code was removed, and customers were contacted directly.
key_facts: About 178 websites were hit by the malicious cyber attack.
Sites affected include BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France, IKEA, Zoom, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger, Peacock.
Hackers injected corrupted JavaScript into Optimizely's platform.
Attack sought to steal credit card numbers, cryptocurrency, and infect Apple devices.
Attacker received about $7,040 in crypto within nine hours on November 16.
Security researcher Scott Helme first uncovered the hack.
Most malicious code was removed from affected sites.
Optimizely blocked the vulnerability, removed code, and contacted customers.
cards.blurb: Nearly 200 major websites, including BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, were targeted by a malicious cyber attack seeking to steal financial information.
cards.spoken: A malicious cyber attack has hit nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA. Hackers injected corrupted JavaScript code into tools from Optimizely, a digital platform used by major companies. The goal was to steal credit card numbers and cryptocurrency and to infect Apple devices. About 178 sites were affected. Security researcher Scott Helme first uncovered the hack and posted about it on Monday. The attacker's crypto wallets received about $7,040 within roughly nine hours on November 16. Most of the malicious code has been removed. Optimizely says it identified and contained the incident, blocked the vulnerable path, removed the code and contacted customers. This attack matters because it involved many major websites and sought to steal financial information.
